close_reason: Added TimeZoneRule::validate_recurrence_overrides_empty() returning Result<(), RecurrenceOverridesError> as opt-in check for the RFC 8984 §4.7.2 'PatchObject value MUST be the empty patch' constraint. Error variant carries the offending wire key for diagnostics. Same pattern as Link::validate_source / Participant::validate_roles. Documented the gap on the recurrence_overrides field. Did not encode via a NonEmptyPatchObject typestate because partial in-flight values still need to round-trip cleanly per RFC 8984 §4.5.2 preserve-mandate. Added time_zone_rule_validate_recurrence_overrides_rejects_non_empty test with 3 cases (None, all-empty, one-non-empty).
description:
**Contract risk**: `TimeZoneRule.recurrence_overrides` is typed as

    Option<HashMap<LocalDateTime, PatchObject>>

with a docstring explicitly saying \"the PatchObject value MUST be
the empty JSON object (`{}`) per RFC 8984 §4.7.2.\" The
`time_zone_rule_recurrence_overrides_round_trips` test asserts this
on deserialize for the spec example input.

But the type permits a non-empty `PatchObject` value:

    let bad: TimeZoneRule = serde_json::from_value(json!({
        \"@type\": \"TimeZoneRule\",
        \"start\": \"1970-01-01T00:00:00\",
        \"offsetFrom\": \"+0000\",
        \"offsetTo\": \"+0000\",
        \"recurrenceOverrides\": {
            \"1990-04-01T02:00:00\": { \"offsetTo\": \"+0100\" }
        }
    })).unwrap();
    // succeeds; the PatchObject is non-empty and the type doesn't care.

**What goes wrong for callers**:
- A server-side caller building a `TimeZoneRule` can silently produce
  spec-non-conformant wire output by inserting any PatchObject they
  like. The contract docstring promises empty; the type system
  doesn't help enforce.
- A client-side caller reading a `TimeZoneRule` cannot assume the
  patch is empty just because the docstring says \"MUST be\". They
  have to defensively check.

**Fix shape** (breaking change):
Option A: change the value type to a unit struct
`EmptyPatchPlaceholder` that round-trips as `{}` only:

    #[non_exhaustive]
    #[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct EmptyPatchPlaceholder {}

    pub recurrence_overrides: Option<HashMap<LocalDateTime, EmptyPatchPlaceholder>>;

This encodes the MUST-be-empty constraint in the type system.
Breaking only for callers that have constructed non-empty patches.
Option B: keep `PatchObject` but add a custom Deserialize that
returns an error on non-empty input. Breaking only for the case
that should never happen.
Option C: leave as-is. Cheapest; least correct.

Lower priority than Link.href/blob_id because the case is rarer
in practice (time-zone rules are mostly auto-generated from
tz-data and unlikely to ship arbitrary patches), but the contract
is the same shape: type permits values the spec forbids.
title: TimeZoneRule.recurrence_overrides value type is PatchObject but RFC 8984 §4.7.2 says it MUST be the empty patch — type permits non-empty patches that the wire spec forbids
